title: Cash Management Standard for Property Charge Advance Repayment Receipts
content:
The receipt terms below govern how money paid toward a Property Charge Advance Repayment arrearage is taken in, applied and referenced, and how the arrangement treats new advances and new charges while it runs.

## Terms by arrangement

| Arrangement | Prepayment penalty | New advance added and installment recomputed over the remaining term | Borrower keeps paying new property charges on time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lump-Sum Repayment | 0.00 percent | No | Yes |
| Repayment Plan - 12 Months | 0.00 percent | Yes | Yes |
| Repayment Plan - 24 Months | 0.00 percent | Yes | Yes |
| Repayment Plan - 36 Months | 0.00 percent | Yes | Yes |
| Repayment Plan - 60 Months | 0.00 percent | Yes | Yes |
| At-Risk Extension | 0.00 percent | No | Yes |

## Terms identical in every arrangement

| Term | Value for the Lump-Sum Repayment, every Repayment Plan and the At-Risk Extension |
|---|---|
| Accepted payment methods | ACH; check; money order |
| Payment smaller than the installment | Applied, and the installment still counts as missed |
| Payment larger than the installment | Applied to the arrearage, reducing the final installments |
| Order of application within the arrangement | Oldest advance first |
| How a repayment reaches the loan | Applied to the loan balance as a prepayment |
| When the arrangement is complete | When the arrearage balance is zero |
| Reference recorded for each repayment | The payment confirmation number |

## Points of application

- No penalty attaches to repaying the arrearage early; the penalty rate is 0 in every arrangement.
- Within an arrangement a payment is applied to the oldest advance first.
- Every repayment is applied to the loan balance as a prepayment, so it lowers the loan balance as well as the arrearage.
- Recomputing the installment over the remaining term when a new advance arrives applies only where installments exist, that is, in the four Repayment Plan arrangements.

### Hypothetical application

Suppose a hypothetical arrearage made up of an older advance of 900.00 and a newer advance of 1400.00 receives a payment of 1000.00 by check. The payment first clears the older advance of 900.00 and applies the remaining 100.00 to the newer one, leaving an arrearage of 1300.00; the same 1000.00 is applied to the loan balance as a prepayment and is recorded under its payment confirmation number. The amounts are illustrative only.
